comments.text: Hello! This is Pt. 1, The Beginning. *Please tell me all the greatest deals you know of in clothing, and we'll get Pt. 2 rolling ASAP* happy Monday!

Thing you pay for:
1.  Human Labor
2. Materials
3. Design
4. Prestige

Snail if you are not aware of the used market for mens suits and ties, that is probably the single most insane & value laden area in all of mensware. The used market for canali/brioni/zegna (and so on, basically all brands outside of some very famous labels like Tom Ford, Brunello) etc is essentially nonexistent. You can get suits w/ an MSRP of $5k+ for $150 and $300 ties for 20 bucks. It doesn't quite fit your mens heritage wear angle given it's more formal wear, but it is a baffling niche of menswear shopping.

So I recently made 2 purchases. I bought the Danny Ace selvedge denim jack from Nudie jeans on a rare sale for about $350 CAD (MSRP $650 CAD). But before that I also bought a raw denim jacket from Lakeside Label for $170 CAD. I checked out reviews of that company after the fact and it basically appeard to be a dropshipping scam with garbage quality clothing, so I planned to return it when it showed up. It came yesterday and it was somehow almost identical quality to the Nudie! It was actual selvedge too (not even advertised as such). Had a nice red stripe selvedge ID, chain stitching, 100% Cotton, was a bit hairy, a bit neppy, and just slightly slubby. The construction and tickness almost identical to the Nudie and was made in China. Not only that, it actually fit me better than the Nudie so now I'm keeping the random China brand and selling the Nudie. It's actually shocking the quality range coming out of China. 

Sidenote: Lakeside label clothing in general appears to be shitty but might have got lucky having old shuttle looms in whatever factory was producing the jacket.

Awesome vid as always. Just want to give a little input on LA apparel. Im a screen printer and like your friend, LA is also my blanks supplier. They make good money, have great benefits, and as far as Dov goes, they dont see too much of him. Seems hes not as gung ho as he used to be in the american apparel days. They have become super fashionable here,  I've evn got a few compliments from people in their 20s, which is nice. 

I also found a dark used  pair of '70 Lee jeans, they are the perfect cut I remember, they drape so well and break a bit at the knee like a straight leg jean should, but don't these days when wore high by the young'uns. The denim is great, nice to have the same quality as the current  Lee 101 at a quarter of the price.
